To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wFROC method provides a reliable and accurate way to evaluate the performance of automatic volcano detection algorithms, and that the wFROCs indicate that automatic volcano detection algorithms perform better than human experts.

(1) the wFROC method provides a principled and statistically valid approach for assessing the performance of an algorithm when the ground truth is subjective, (2) the wFROCs can be used to compare the performance of human and automatic algorithms, and (3) the uncertainty in ground truth must be considered in any assessment of algorithm performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of wFROC analysis to assess the relative performance of human and automatic algorithms in a difficult remote sensing application.
the problem of evaluating the performance of automated analysis algorithms on remote sensing imagery when the "ground-truth" is subjective.
the development and evaluation of algorithms for automated analysis of radar imagery, and with the development of new methods for handling lack of verifiable ground-truth data in this application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of weighted FROCs for the assessment of the relative performance of humans and automated algorithms in the presence of lack of ground truth is an effective and practical method.
the wFROC is an appropriate and useful tool for evaluating the relative performance of human and automatic systems when the "ground-truth" is subjective.
the wFROC is a useful tool in the evaluation of automated analysis of SAR imagery when ground truth is uncertain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a methodology to assess the uncertainty in the ground truth and to evaluate the relative performance of humans and algorithms.
the lack of ground truth is a problem in remote sensing.
